title: The Global Grammar of Swearing: A Cross-Linguistic Atlas of Taboo, Insult, and Profanity
domain: linguistics / psycholinguistics / sociolinguistics / cross-cultural psychology / linguistic typology / cultural evolution
summary: A falsification-first cross-linguistic program testing which properties of taboo language are stable across communities, genealogically structured, or context-sensitive. Phase 0 now audits the open 18-community/13-language Sulpizio et al. dataset, exposes substantial cross-lab annotation heterogeneity, introduces an orthogonal multi-axis ontology, links samples to Glottolog, and builds reproducible harmonization and reliability gates before any cultural-prevalence claim.

dependencies.011: evidence provenance, applicability-aware review and abstention semantics

aris.provenance: ARIS4C guided design with live prior-art audit; confirmatory empirical run not yet frozen
